card.name: Past-tense verb after 'most cases'
card.fires_on: The past-tense verb (was, occurred, received, had been) right after a subject like 'most cases', 'these reactions' or 'there' in a report about what happened to patients.

modes.label: Verb after cases/reactions
modes.description: Past-tense verb such as occurred or followed right after 'cases' or 'reactions' in adverse event summaries.
modes.example: Most cases<< occurred>> in patients with renal impairment who did not

modes.label: Past-tense was/had after subject
modes.description: A form of was or had been after a subject describing past events.
modes.example: clomipramine hydrochloride<< had>> been administered with other epileptogenic agents

card.writes: It promotes past-tense 'was' and 'did' and suppresses 'now', pushing toward past-tense narration of what happened.
card.plain: It fires where a sentence is describing what happened in past cases, just after the subject and before the past-tense verb.
